title: Best Internal Developer Platforms for Infrastructure Self-Service in 2026
summary: A ranked list of the best internal developer platforms for infrastructure self-service: Massdriver, Port, Backstage, Humanitec, Spacelift, and Terraform Cloud, compared on provisioning, guardrails, and setup effort.
body_markdown:
Developers should be able to get a database, a queue, or a whole environment without filing a ticket. Platform teams should be able to allow that without handing out cloud credentials or becoming the approval bottleneck. The requester now might be a developer, a CI pipeline, or a coding agent, and the internal developer platform (IDP) you pick decides whether every one of them reaches production through one governed path or through several.


This list ranks six tools by how well they deliver governed infrastructure self-service on top of the Terraform, OpenTofu, and Helm your platform team already writes. We build Massdriver, so it is number one. We explain why, and we say where each of the others is the better choice.


## How we ranked them


Every tool here claims some form of self-service. We scored them on five questions:


1. **Does it provision infrastructure itself?** Or does it hand the request to a pipeline you build and maintain?
2. **Where do guardrails apply?** Before a request is accepted, or after the plan is written? Does the requester ever hold cloud credentials?
3. **Can a developer use it without knowing IaC?** Or does self-service mean writing Terraform or YAML?
4. **How much does the platform team build before developers see value?**
5. **Does it keep your existing modules?** Or do you rewrite them for the new tool?


## The ranking at a glance

## 1. Massdriver


**Best for:** platform teams that want developers, CI, and AI agents to provision infrastructure through one governed path, using the Terraform, OpenTofu, and Helm they already have.


Massdriver is a platform orchestrator with a developer portal included. Your platform team defines approved infrastructure once: existing IaC published as bundles, with a schema for the inputs a requester may set and the policy that applies. Developers and agents then assemble environments from that catalog through the UI, CLI, API, or MCP server. The requester proposes; the platform validates and executes. Terraform stays the source of infrastructure implementation, and agents work through it instead of calling the cloud directly.


What puts it first:


- **It provisions the infrastructure.** Massdriver generates the pipeline for each deploy, runs it, and records the result. There is no separate automation layer to build.
- **Guardrails apply before execution.** Inputs are constrained by schema, and policy, scoped permissions, and environment-specific approvals are evaluated before every apply. Dev can move quickly while production requires extra sign-off.
- **Requesters get capabilities, not cloud credentials.** Massdriver executes with credentials the developer or agent never holds, and every change is attributable and auditable.
- **Developers draw what they need.** The canvas and config forms need no YAML or IaC knowledge.
- **Your modules move as they are.** Existing Terraform and OpenTofu are published as bundles. Resource import brings running infrastructure under management without a redeploy.
- **Typed dependencies show the blast radius.** Typed inputs, outputs, and artifacts feed a dependency graph, so you can see what consumes what and what a change may affect.
- **Day-two operations come included.** State, access control, cost tracking, preview environments, and environment graphs ship with the platform, and it can be self-hosted inside your own environment.


**Limits:** Massdriver is opinionated about the bundle as the unit of the platform. Teams that want to hand-build every layer of their IDP will find less to assemble.


[See pricing](https://www.massdriver.cloud/pricing) or[put one real infrastructure change through the governed path](https://www.massdriver.cloud/demo) .


## 2. Port


**Best for:** organizations whose main problem is visibility across hundreds of services, with provisioning already handled elsewhere.


Port is an internal developer portal, and a good one to put in front of an execution layer. It offers a software catalog, scorecards, and self-service actions exposed as forms. The actions call external systems such as CI pipelines and Terraform runs, so the platform team builds and maintains that automation.


**Strengths:** flexible data model, good catalog and scorecards, fast to stand up as a front door.


**Limits:** Port does not provision. Scorecards measure compliance after deployment instead of preventing a bad request. Port and Massdriver work together: point Port's actions at the Massdriver API and Port stays the portal while Massdriver is the execution layer underneath.


Read the full[Port vs Massdriver](https://www.massdriver.cloud/comparisons/port-vs-massdriver) comparison.


## 3. Backstage


**Best for:** teams with a dedicated platform group, a mature provisioning pipeline, and a discovery problem.


Backstage is the open source portal framework from Spotify, now a CNCF project. It provides a software catalog, scaffolder templates, TechDocs, and a plugin system. It runs nothing itself: when a template appears to create infrastructure, it calls a CI job, a script, or a Terraform run somewhere else.


**Strengths:** free, extensible, large plugin ecosystem, and strong for service discovery.


**Limits:** you host, upgrade, and extend it. Every new resource type needs a template, a workflow, and a module, and policy ends up spread across all three. Massdriver publishes a[Backstage plugin](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@massdriver/backstage-plugin) so Backstage can stay the interface in front of a working execution layer.


Read the full[Backstage vs Massdriver](https://www.massdriver.cloud/comparisons/backstage-vs-massdriver) comparison.


## 4. Humanitec


**Best for:** teams that want a framework to build a custom IDP around the Score workload specification and have the engineering capacity to do it.


Humanitec is a platform orchestrator. Platform teams write Resource Definitions and Drivers that map a workload's needs to real infrastructure, and developers describe workloads in Score.


**Strengths:** fine-grained control and a clear model for workload-centric platforms.


**Limits:** platform teams write and maintain definitions for every resource type before developers get value. Deployments still route through pipeline integrations, and developers work with YAML workload specs.


Read the full[Humanitec vs Massdriver](https://www.massdriver.cloud/comparisons/humanitec-vs-massdriver) comparison.


## 5. Spacelift


**Best for:** platform and DevOps teams managing many Terraform, OpenTofu, or Pulumi projects who want governance over runs.


Spacelift improves Terraform execution: it runs IaC from Git, adds policy as code with Open Policy Agent, and manages dependencies between stacks.


**Strengths:** strong policy engine, stack dependencies, and multi-tool IaC support.


**Limits:** it assumes the person who wants infrastructure writes IaC, pushes to Git, and waits for a run. That fits the platform team's own infrastructure. For developers asking for a database, it is still a queue. Policies act after the plan is written. Teams moving from Spacelift keep their modules, since they publish to Massdriver as bundles.


Read the full[Spacelift vs Massdriver](https://www.massdriver.cloud/comparisons/spacelift-vs-massdriver) comparison.


## 6. Terraform Cloud


**Best for:** operations teams that live in Terraform and want one place to run it, with remote state and Sentinel policy.


Terraform Cloud is HashiCorp's hosted runner, and like Spacelift it improves how Terraform executes. Massdriver instead reduces how many people and systems need to operate Terraform directly. It provides remote state, VCS-driven runs, run history, and Sentinel.


**Strengths:** the most direct path for a Terraform-only shop, with state handled for you.


**Limits:** it runs Terraform and no other IaC, such as Helm. No-code provisioning offers a form per module, but the experience is still workspaces, HCL, and the operations team in the middle. Sentinel checks the plan, so violations surface late. Preview environments need scripting.


Read the full[Terraform Cloud vs Massdriver](https://www.massdriver.cloud/comparisons/terraform-cloud-vs-massdriver) comparison.


## Which one should you pick?


If your situation is... Start with


Developers, CI, and agents all need infrastructure and you own Terraform Massdriver


Provisioning works, and you need a catalog and scorecards Port or Backstage


You want to build a custom IDP from a framework Humanitec


Your platform team needs governance over many IaC stacks Spacelift


You run only Terraform and want a hosted runner Terraform Cloud


These tools are not all exclusive. A portal in front of Massdriver gives you a catalog and an orchestrator that provisions from it. Whichever you choose, the platform team does the hard work once, and every future change inherits the controls.
